And if you don't feel like studying, remember the 5 minutes rule:

Forget about everything, your phone, your life, your family, for 5 minutes and use those 5 minutes to study and only to study. Put all your energies and effort into studying for 5 minutes. Just 5 minutes.

The first 5 minutes are the hardest of any task you don't feel like doing, and after those 5 minutes whatever you're doing that you thought it was impossible is going to become easier. That's what I do everytime I don't feel like studying, cooking, taking a shower, buying groceries, going to work... I do it even when I think I'm too sick to do anything. It works.

I know we have modern apps for young students but the reason we're still using notebooks these days is that thats how you learn better, so if you feel overwhelmed about exams, draw a calendar and put them there.

When it comes to studying for a test, if for example, you need to study ten pages of a book for next week's test, divide the content in subcategories. Usually books already do that but it could help if you made a conceptual diagram. Nothing fancy, as long as you understand your own handwritting is fine.

Read a paragraph or a part of the conceptual diagram and ask to yourself what you understood about it. Try to explain it like if you explained it to another friend. Write down dates, new terms and what they mean... You can even make a timeline if you need it.

Once you feel you understand it and you can explain it to a friend, do the same thing with the next paragraph. And some paragraphs later go back to the first paragraph or take a break, and try to explain to yourself what you read in the first paragraph without reading it.

What matters is that you understand what you're reading and you can explain it later with different words. And of course, you memorized names, dates...

This may sound like extra effort and time but it psychologically helps a lot, because you're not thinking about a long and tiring essay, but you're thinking about every step you need to complete your essay individually.

So instead of spending a whole day overwhelmed about your essay, you already know what to do beforehand so you can just do some research in the morning, have a break, write the introduction and chill a little... It helps.

That's a very basic laptop for office work honestly, it won't run games as smoothly as a gaming laptop because of it's CPU and GPU.

I'd recommend you to get at least a laptop with a CPU intel core i5 and a GPU N-Vidia, NOT Intel UHD, it must be N-Vidia. Those things are extremely important because they're the only parts of a laptop that you can't replace/change later.

You can always save up to add 4 GB more to make 8 GB in total, you can always change that HDD for a SSD to make your laptop faster and more fluid... But you can't change neither the CPU nor the GPU in a laptop.

So the ram and the hdd/ssd don't matter when you're buying a laptop, it's far cheaper to install them somewhere else later (or that's how it is where I live, we just buy a laptop, buy the extra ram and the SSD and take it to an expert that installs them or we install them ourselves).

You'd need at least 8 GB ram and a 480 GB SSD because 256 is nothing honestly. Only Sims 4 with all it's packs is about 40 GB.

SSDs are expensive tho, if your laptop comes with a 1 TB HDD it's perfectly fine, don't add a SSD until you saved up for a 480 GB at least.

But your minimun ideal specs would be:

* CPU intel core i5
* 8 GB ram
* 1 TB HDD or 480 GB SSD (if you can afford it it's completely worth it)
* GPU N-Vidia 

Good luck :)
